THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 24.07.2014 in M.V.C.No.115/2012 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Kolar ('the Tribunal'
for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 27.05.2012 at about 03:00 pm while the petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40/H-7670 near Stone Crusher Factory on Gowribidanur-Hudugur Road, hit by a Tata Sumo bearing Reg.No.KA-04/N- 9224 from the opposite direction, injuring him.
After taking treatment, he has approached the NC: 2023:KHC:41304 Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest of 12% p.a.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal after taking evidence of both parties awarded compensation of Rs.2,03,400/- Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Smt. Suguna.

R. Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. R.
Govindarajan, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was aged 22 years, as a coolie, he was earning Rs.300/- per day.
He had suffered 2 major fractures inflicting permanent disability, affecting his earning capacity.
He was laid-up for longer period, spent huge money towards treatment, but the Tribunal did not consider the compensation in proportionate to the injury and the NC: 2023:KHC:41304 disability
, the Tribunal has assessed the disability as against the medical evidence and taken income at Rs.4,000/- and she sought for enhancement.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner has suffered simple fractures, after treatment fracture was united.
Evidence is lead suggesting 36% of limb disability, which is on the higher side and the Tribunal has rightly taken 10% whole body disability.
In the year 2012, the Tribunal has correctly assessed Rs.4,000/- for a Coolie and there is no necessity for enhancement of compensation and he supported the impugned judgment.

sentences.text:
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8.
There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

Medical record shows that the NC: 2023:KHC:41304 petitioner has sustained open fracture of Olicranon, open fracture of right 2nd, 3rd, 4th metatarsals shaft apart from injury to the head and right elbow.
PW-2 Dr. P.V. Manohar has given opinion that the petitioner has suffered 30% and 6% limb disability for the 2 fractures and whole body disability at 12%
; the Tribunal has considered it at 10%.
The petitioner was treated at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and also at St. John's Hospital, Bengaluru.
He was inpatient in the hospital for 18 days.
Assessment of disability at 10% by the Tribunal is proper.
9. The petitioner is aged 22 years and he was a Coolie, earning Rs.300/- per day, but there is no proof of it.
Even if the petitioner is treated as a person with no proof of income in the year 2010, he will earn not less than Rs.6,000/- per month.
Hence, the income taken by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

On perusal of the impugned judgment, it is pertinent to note that the Tribunal has awarded NC: 2023:KHC:41304 Rs.30,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.52,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards food and nourishment, Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities, Rs.86,400/- towards loss of future earnings, in all Rs.2,03,400/-.

In view of the above discussions, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows: Rs.30,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.52,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.6,000/- towards attendant charges,
Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomfort, Rs.10,000/- towards food and nourishment,
Rs.5,000/- towards travelling expenses, Rs.24,000/- towards loss of income during laid-up for 4 months (Rs.6,000/- x 4).
Loss of future income will be Rs.6,000/- + Rs.2,400/- (40% future prospects) = Rs.8,400/- x 12 x 18 x 10% = Rs.1,81,440/-.
Then, total compensation comes to Rs.3,38,440/- as against Rs.2,03,400/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.1,35,040/-, rounded off to Rs.1,35,000/-.
This is the just compensation that NC: 2023:KHC:41304 the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii) Impugned judgment is modified.

iii)Petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,35,000/- with interest of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, excluding interest for the delayed period of 171 days in filing the appeal.
iv)The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
